Maneuvering

Manobra de Paragem Rápida

Emergency procedure whereby engine is set full astern and helm hard over to rapidly stop vessel’s forward motion within minimum distance.

Questions and answers

Questions and answers

What is Manobra de Paragem Rápida?

In this glossary, Manobra de Paragem Rápida refers to: Emergency procedure whereby engine is set full astern and helm hard over to rapidly stop vessel’s forward motion within minimum distance.

How is Manobra de Paragem Rápida used in maritime?

In maritime communication, this term appears in contexts such as: "Passarela: Inicie a manobra de paragem rápida, toda ré e leme todo a bombordo, homem ao mar na través de estibordo."

Why does Manobra de Paragem Rápida matter in maritime?

Manobra de Paragem Rápida matters because it supports clear communication in Maneuvering contexts for Deck Officers, Engine Officers, and Masters. It also connects to aviation training and exam language such as STCW, Marlins Test, ISF Watchkeeper, and GMDSS.

Who uses Manobra de Paragem Rápida?

Manobra de Paragem Rápida is mainly used by Deck Officers, Engine Officers, and Masters.

Definition

Emergency procedure whereby engine is set full astern and helm hard over to rapidly stop vessel’s forward motion within minimum distance.

Operational example

Bridge: Commence quick stop manoeuvre, full astern and hard port, person overboard on starboard beam.

Localized term

Manobra de Paragem Rápida
